setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Named by the prospect and confirmed by the rep with a full note read-back: "I was talking with Kim." / "You talked with Kim, I don't know, three days ago, something like that, yeah?... So he briefed me in on your situation that you're 37, right? You're working in management mostly... And you're training five, six a day on your own, doing, like, split plus cardio. Is that accurate?" No suffix in the title, but the setter is unambiguous from content.

prospect.name: Sako
prospect.occupation: Management role at a corporate office. Standing desk, so alternates sitting and standing; starts early and leaves around 5pm. Not a business owner — "I don't have any, any other job besides this one job."
prospect.family_status: Single, wants a partner. Visits his mother and sister about once a week.
prospect.training_background: Trains six times a week at the gym, 8:00-8:30pm for an hour and a half to two hours — lifting, not heavy, plus about 30 minutes of treadmill cardio added in the last month. Self-programmed splits with no structure behind them. Reports feeling he has lost weight and gained a couple of pounds of muscle recently, though he does not weigh himself. Some morning yoga.
prospect.medical: Self-administering weekly testosterone injections for about two months, started for energy, and reports the level is now elevated: "my testosterone is a little bit high, so I need to, like, not take it all the time, because of the injection." Mild lower-back stiffness on waking that resolves within a couple of minutes after yoga; no pain during the rest of the day. No injuries or movement limitations reported. Sleeping five to six hours a night (midnight to about 06:45) and requiring a 10-15 minute nap after work to have the energy to train. Drinks almost no water, mostly black coffee, plus one or two Diet Cokes a day. Eats close to bedtime.

signals: Already training hard and consistently — six sessions a week, two hours each — with the discipline the rep explicitly credited: "you got the discipline, most people don't have that"

Frames the ask as good to great, not rescue: "My body is not bad. It's just like, I feel like I need a better, like I want to have a better body. And even my nutrition is not the worst compared like to other people, but I want to just improve it"

Driven by status and confidence in a fitness-saturated market: "the lifestyle in Los Angeles, like in California, everybody's very addicted to like gym, they work out, and they have pretty nice bodies, and I like that"
Already spending on physique and energy optimisation — two months into self-administered TRT

Departs from the pure optimizer on one point: price was a real hesitation ("6,000, it's a little bit too much"), though he also conceded "it's not too bad, too" and disclosed a $2,500 monthly surplus and five-figure savings

goals.text: Lose the soft lower belly — the one part of his body that is not toned
Build a stronger, better-looking body overall
Feel 100% confident taking his shirt off at a party or a beach without doubting himself
Find a partner; believes his shape is part of why he is still single
Be genuinely healthier and know what he is putting in his body
Match the physique standard of the LA community he moves in — "I want that too, before it's too late"
A programme with actual logic to it rather than self-assembled splits and cardio

On-off nutrition cycle with binges — ate a pound of feta cheese in a day — followed by resolutions to stop
Confidence hit from the soft lower belly, which he directly links to being single
Two-hour sessions six times a week with no programme logic and unclear results
Eats late — around 11pm — and then cannot sleep hungry, so eats again before bed
Barely drinks water; runs the day on black coffee plus one or two Diet Cokes
Weekly family meals he cannot eat clean at, and leaves feeling bad about
Energy collapses after work, which he is currently managing with testosterone injections

objections.raw_quote: I will have to think about this. And then get back to you, is that the final prize?
objections.rep_response: Ran the play properly and at length — the belief question ("do you feel that can actually get you to leaner body, to have that big body and make you more confident and finally hit your goals?"), the follow-up ("What makes you feel it can?"), the blocker probe ("what's actually coming up for you right now that's preventing you from getting started?") and the scripted line "thinking is not the problem. Deciding is." Then isolated it to money.

objections.raw_quote: I'm just going to think about it. 6,000, it's a little bit too much.
objections.rep_response: Ran the open-wallet play through to a full financial picture — monthly surplus, savings, investments and credit cards — then stepped away to consult and came back with two structures: $3,000 today plus $1,000 a month for three months, or six monthly payments of $1,200 totalling $7,200.

objections.raw_quote: And also, like, I have vacation planned. So it's like more money to spend, I would say.
objections.rep_response: Ran a priorities reframe: "This is two separate things about setting yourself a priority, whether vacation is a priority or your goals, your physique, and your health that you want to improve" and "vacation is going to be next year, two years after, and so on... you can show up for your vacation right now in way better shape."

objections.raw_quote: I just have to see like how credited you are. Like, I just can't proceed forward without, like, I can't pay anything right now... I need to do like more research. Like, I just can't pay you right now. I just have to see like the website, all the reviews and everything before I, so give me some time
objections.rep_response: Told him he would not get back in touch and was looking for a way out, then argued that anything he found online could be fake — including testimonials — and that Trevor would be in jail if the business were a scam. No verification material was offered.

tiers.note: "An investment for that is 6K." Confirmed as final when asked: "is that the final prize?" / "It is."
Split: $3,000 today, then $1,000 a month for three months. Explicitly no interest. Obtained by the rep stepping away mid-call to consult.
Off-menu: six monthly payments of $1,200, total $7,200. $1,200 above the stated price. The prospect caught the discrepancy — "$7,000 or you said $6,000?"

offer.payment_plan_terms: Two options presented after the rep left the call to consult: (1) $3,000 down today plus $1,000 per month for three months, no interest, total $6,000; (2) six payments of $1,200 per month, total $7,200. Neither was accepted.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: "the whole transformation takes six months, and there's a guarantee on this, yeah? Because if you won't hit the goals in six months, Trevor will work with you for free until you hit them." Note that this states the guarantee against the prospect's goals generally, which is materially broader than the strength-specific version (+8 kg on baseline kettlebell weight) the same rep gave on 30 June.

prospect_financials.note: Disclosed live: about $2,500 left at the end of the month after bills and groceries; savings he confirmed as five-figure when prompted with "$10,000, $15,000?" but declined to specify; no crypto, stocks or other investments; holds credit cards but pays them off in full before interest accrues.

evidence: No decision and no payment. Held the line through a sustained close attempt: "No, I have to think about it. This is a huge decision I have to make."
Follow-up booked for 3pm on 9 July with a calendar invite to be emailed, and the rep sending a text so the prospect has his number.
Positive signal: he did not reject the offer and said the money is workable — "I said it's doable. Like, it's not like, oh, it's the way I cannot do it" — and "I like the program. I like the guy."
Counter-evidence: the real blocker is trust, not money. He asked to check the website and reviews and was told those could all be fake, which is unlikely to have improved his position.
Counter-evidence: he leaves on vacation the following day, so the 9 July follow-up lands after a competing discretionary spend.
outcome.next_step: Follow-up call booked for 3pm on 9 July 2026; invite to be emailed and the rep to text his number. Prospect on vacation from the following day and intends to research the company before deciding.

notable.note: Process-wise this is the strongest call in the batch — a full setter note read-back, eight of nine baseline checks, a textbook reflect-back, and the only complete open-wallet financial picture anywhere in these twelve files — and it is also the one with the most serious conduct and clinical exposure. The prospect volunteered that he is two months into self-administered weekly testosterone injections with a level he describes as already elevated; the rep's response was "but you know you can do that naturally", followed by an unqualified claim that peptides accelerate undetected cancer cells. When the prospect asked to check the company's website and reviews before paying, the rep told him testimonials could all be fake and accused him of looking for an easy way out. Nobody at any point asked whether a clinician had cleared him to train, or whether his prescriber knew.
